newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE white sugar down, March baulks at resistance.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE white sugar down, March baulks at resistance.

text.p: White sugar futures backed off earlier highs in a listless Monday session as the London market kept pace with the slight weakness in the raws, keeping the white premium steady, traders said.

The spot March contract briefly nudged up to $300 resistance before the New York open but a disappointing performance on the raws prompted commission house selling in London to erase the earlier strength seen from trade purchases. At 1644 GMT March was down $1.20 at $298.60 and May down 90 cents at $298.50. Volume reached 1,117 lots. Technically, March looks to be forming a small upward channel back towards $300 in a corrective move from last week's fierce arbitrage-led selling bout.

Traders said activity on the whites market was likely to be quiet in the run-up to Europe's Christmas holiday period but noted that current low prices could draw some pre-Ramadan buying by Middle East players.
"I think we'll have the odd busy day but until Christmas comes it'll be a bit sporadic," said one trader.

Elsewhere, physical news was thin on the ground although traders cited market talk that the Philippines might have to export 200,000 tonnes of sugar, possibly whites, early in 1997 due to over-importing and low internal prices.
Paris positions were weaker but turnover was light at a total 359 lots. March was down $1.00 at $299.00 and May down 50 cents at $298.50.
